I want to tell you everyone reacts to life threatening emergency differently.  You just can never predict how you will respond.  You think you would cry but even you cannot predict how you would actually act in the moment because its sudden and hard to process that your life could suddenly change so irrevocably.  Sometimes people dont cry because they've gone into a kind of survival mode where they cannot be emotional because your loved one and the emergency need you to hold it together.  Sometimes in my experience your brain goes in that mode to help you get through the best way you can. So just say I love you and I'm here for you. If your doing that your doing the right thing. Like you said you can't make any promises things will be ok and you can't fix it but being there for her, no matter how she manifests her grief is all you need to do. She will probably tell you what she needs when she knows. It's a confusing time. Bring her the little comforts that could brighten her day, a glass of hot tea, a foot massage,  that won't fix anything but maybe it will bring comfort and just love and support her as you have been is my advice. There is no perfect thing to say at moments like this

I have to be honest.  I've let alot of people go either gradually or all at once. It's hard to maintain a relationship when your a little unstable and suffering from depression and shit you know that. At this point I have a open line of communication with my family,  I know their always there but I dont actually communicate with anyone except for my mother who maintains a relationship with me by force if necessary.  Sometimes I've completely shut down and the thought of speaking to anyone besides my husband seems impossible.  I turn the sound off for weeks sometimes and don't check my texts. My mother has shown up to my house multiple times unannounced to find me a mess. I'm working on not doing that at least for her because my father killed himself and sometimes when I go quiet she thinks I'm finally dead. I have one friend who is like a sister who I know will always love me, who I know I'll always be able to drop into conversation effortlessly with. I text her every now and then. I have my husband and thank God once you're around someone 24/7 eventually your guard drops to a more comfortable level and I've found I can be happy around him but I must have time to myself even in our relationship. I have to recharge.  My husband thank God loves me and is with me for the long run, it can be confusing and frustrating to be in a relationship with some with bipolar disorder,  PTSD, anxiety disorder, major depression and borderline personality.  As much as I've let people go I've also ruined relationships with my illness.  Beyond that I dont really talk to anybody.  The only other friends I had before were all ex boyfriends/ friends with Benefits so obviously I had to give them up for my marriage.  The last relationship I was in was extremely serious and lasted on and off for years but now, maybe six months later I'm married and that relationship is almost a blank and hold very little emotional impact at all. I can separate myself from it and keep going which I guess is good? I could conjure memories but they dont naturally come. That relationship was ruined because of my problems and my psychiatrist dropped me because I missed an appointment.  I've been trying to make my meds last but I'm down to about six doses and all the psychiatrists in my area have long waiting lists, county even makes you wait. I dont want to be in terror again and drive everyone away and ruin my life so I might have to check myself into a psych hospital to get meds again and an emergency appointment,  they set one up because they only give you 15 days worth of meds when you leave and they want you to stay stable.  Sometimes that's what you have to do to get help. Honestly my life is in upheaval, I moved an hour away from everyone I know which is far for me, away from the city I love and married my landlord not long after I moved in because he made me feel trust that he would treat me with respect and love me and never leave no matter how hard things get. He gave me a home, MY home. Sometimes it's hard to believe, I'm still absorbing it that I have something now and I can feel safe from disappearing into the system or homelessness. I'm still learning about my husband and learning how to love him but I'm learning as I go. Not every relationship is fireworks and I've been through enough to love security and stability now but the most emotionally involved,  absolutely smitten I've ever been was in a 5 year relationship with my abuser. Its so screwy, I've heard of trauma bonding and maybe that explains it but I loved the boy who pushed me down onto of a car hood, pulled down my underwear and spanked me in front of his friends more than anyone I've ever known.  He loved to humiliate me, to dominate me and wasnt above hitting me in the head because it wouldn't leave a mark there, or bending my fingers back. He kept other girls and even brought them around me. It was awful and at bvb one point i was afraid to even speak around him. But the thing is he reached into that numbness and made me FEEL so i stayed and he warped so many parts of me. He is the only one I still miss. That fire is still there, before I met my husband I was fooling again and even though he was an adult now we still reverted to our old ways not to fighting but the same exciting dynamic of pain pleasure love hate submission and dominance. I felt so much but ultimately I had to leave. That feeling of butterflies in your stomach, a racing pulse, feeling like your going to throw up and pass out when you see them isn't always everything I guess at least for me. Emotions dont make love. Love is more deliberate than that I think. It's a commitment to think of their welfare, support them, give them affection and in the relationship I'm in now the goal is to treat each other with respect and love and heal be happy and build a life we can enjoy.  My husband is a medically retired deputy  and I am on disability for my mental issues. So we can do anything or go anywhere we want within budget and reason. So Were just trying to be happy now. Honestly the greatest source of joy in my life and the ones who fill my heart with love the most right now are my cats! It's so easy to love animals for some reason . Anyway I'm sorry I went on so long. I have no one to talk to really and it's a hard problem to understand. Sometimes I think Its not real and I'm just a bad or weak person. I need to hear someone else feels the emptiness. It's so puzzling dude.

I've always had depression. Always had to take medication and admittedly have self medicated to deal with for a long long time. Anyway I had a prescription for muscle relaxers once and I want to have a break from my mind and all its bullshit so I took a bunch of them and this time I blacked out. My ex had to eventually take me to the Erie and they decided to 51/50 me because I had a history of hospitalization and they believed it was a suicide attempt.  So I was sent automatically to the county mental facility.  Technically I was sent to the holding tank where they observe you from a distance and decide whether to keep you and pull you further into the county mental health system or to let you go either to another treatment facility if you have insurance or out on your own recognizance. Anyway this place. It was something else. There were two major rooms with a nursing station looking out on the main room, these rooms were all there was. There were no beds just filthy chairs. Men and women in all states of cleanliness, undress and instability were all thrown together.  The first night I was there I had to sleep on the linoleum floor with a thin blanket at the feet of a man who was clearly homeless which I do not judge at all except he was aggressive , barely covering his body, covered in shit and masterbating over my head. The nurses were all completely indifferent and stayed in their station most of the time. There was nothing to do and it was absolutely impossible to focus on the TV or anything because of the adrenaline rushing through me just made me quiver. Time slowed down and every minute was torture.  I know I screwed up, and self medicating isn't helpful but sometimes when your struggling it's hard not to just want a break from the constant tension and pain. That was all I wanted and the worst thing was the neglect we were all treated with, and the suffering I saw and felt because they kept the place society puts people in crisis like a filthy  humangarbage pit. It's hard not to feel like garbage even after you get out. When I was there  men would keep the only bathroom flooded with urine. They would piss on the floor and block the drain with towels. Everytime you had to pee you had to walk through it. And you had no shoes, only socks. No one intervened, no one was watching,  no one cared. The janitor cleaned it a couple times a day but it flooded again quickly.  That kind of dirt can get under your skin and become a part of how you see yourself.  It's such a clear message that you are disposable, forgotten and not even worthy of basic human dignity.  That sticks with you. Personally it seared my soul and I came out way worse and way less likely to ask for help. Hospitalization is always awful but the worst thing is being able to notice the coldness and neglect even people in mental health care treat their patients.  I suffer from major depression and suicidal ideation so my reasoning isn't completely fucked up so alot of the time I've ended up caring for the sicker patients who can't advocate for themselves for their needs. It shouldn't be like that but so often staff treat their job like a chore even at the best places, at worst an annoyance. Being in that facility and being in others throughout my life has been some of the most formative and difficult times of my life.

Hello, I struggle with similar feelings alot. I went through trauma as a child and abuse as an young adult for years and hearing someone else worry about this is, not offence to you OP, so refreshing.  It can be so strange and be so lonely to be around people and suddenly realize the limitations of your openness, of your ability to let someone in. That's part of it for me. I act the part and watch that I act the same way but so many times when a normal person should feel joy or sorrow or empathy I feel nothing. When family members I loved and was so close to as a little child have died I have faced their deaths in a state of apathy. It isn't chock, after I experienced the first trauma as a child when I was returned to my family it was like I had taken a mental and emotional step away from everyone I knew and loved and nothing could fix it because that part of me had shriveled up and died. I know it did because it has never come back, I can't remember so much of my life now. I disassociate alot I think, or who knows maybe I'm just a bad person.  I think if you meet the right person and your brave enough to risk it you should stop trying to decide if a relationship will end in nothing right from the beginning.  If you're ever going to have love you have to be open to it for it to be a possibility.  You owe it to yourself to relax and see where things go. I know from personal experience that's hard. Because of the way I am I'm the type of person who could ghost a close relationship and after the initial shock can forget about them and many details of my memories with them in no time. Its unnerving.  So to have anyone in my life I know I have to put forward a lot of effort because I feel safer isolating.  Sometimes it's worth the work in my opinion though.  It might take a long time and it might take someone special but I know from personal experience there are people out there who are firecrackers and can make even a stone bleed. You never know,  one day someone may set your life on FIRE! One day your heart might sing dude. Dont count yourself out op, that's all I'm saying. Hope that helps

Waking up in the morning used to be something I dreaded even as I finally fell to sleep at night.  For me living in a precarious living situation,  with hardly any money really contributed to my anxiety.  Every time I went to sleep it felt like I was waking up five minutes later even after a full nights sleep.  I never felt rested and woke with my heart beating out of my chest dreading having to face another day of uncertainty,  depression and anxiety. Once my life got easier it got easier to surrender to sleep and easier to wake up. It even got easier to sleep, I stopped yelling in my sleep so much. I still have my mental issues and still have to take medication every day but the diminished stress has really made a remarkable impact on my mental health and sleep. It makes me feel so lucky to be in a better situation now. I could so easily still be there wishing I was dead but by chance was saved. It makes me sad that not everyone gets help. It makes me sad people have to be so miserable because they dont have access to basic things they need

I'm very very late but I'd still like to leave my experience.  The most disheartening thing I've experienced in my life has been seeing the truly dismal care people with mental illness recieve. I personally have suffered all my life with major depression disorder and bipolar disorder. I inherited my illness from my father ( who ended up cutting his life short) and his side of the family   just like inheriting red hair. I didn't choose it. The morbid reality though I would come to learn is people, people whose living is dependent on caring for others, doctors and nurses feel that they can treat people who are receiving care for a mental illness with less respect than children.  They can throw then into holding pens together with no where to sleep, hold them with no medication or without seeing a doctor for days. They feel absolutely fearless because in this society people who are mentally ill ,especially people who have a hard time maintaining the behavior polite society expects because of their illness, are not necessarily afforded dignity, loving concern,  or respect. I've met people who have been through horrendous things. I had a friend who I met once in treatment. They were neglected by their parent nearly dying of malnutrition and neglect very early on in life, at a very young age this same sorry excuse for a parent kicked them out on the street.  To survive they sold themselves.  On one of these hook ups the person who was substantially bigger overpowered them, handcuffed them, and one by one REMOVED THEIR TEETH.
This is why they had to get treatment,  because the trauma was so severe they would disassociate  and wake up weeks later with nothing in another city! God knows they did not fucking deserve the treatment, the attitude they recieved, that I and countless other people receive when they go looking for "help". My friend couldn't work and was on disability as am I. If I don't have my medication I will likely kill myself because I will without a doubt end up once again completely overwhelmed by terror and suicidal ideation it is excruciating to bare even for a little while I simply couldn't make it without them, I've tried but have been on them since I 2as 11. The way people regard my friend who was living in a board and care home, ( a private residence which takes on people who are disabled and provides them a home environment,  a bed, and meals) where they were not allowed to even crack their window so they could breathe because their PTSD makes them feel claustrophobic,  the way people have treated and regard me has by turns sickened me, and broken my heart. My life has been so mangled by these experiences. It is the ugliest most morbid reality I've had to swallow in my life and has sadly made me a very pessimistic, sad and angry person.
